newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Amcor sees deflation for manufacturers.
newsitem.headline: Amcor sees deflation for manufacturers.

text.p: One of Australia leading businessmen said on Wednesday that the country's manufacturing sector was undergoing a period of deflation as pricing pressure was cutting severly into manufacturers margins.
Don Macfarlane managing director of paper and packaging group Amcor said Australia's economy was boosted by growth in financial services, communications and leisure services.
"The basic manufacturing part of Australian industry I think is undergoing a period of deflation," said Macfarlane, who is the brother of Australia's central bank governor, Ian Macfarlane.
"So it is growing relatively slowly and I would say it is growing not much more than 1.5 (percent), two percent not much more than that," Macfarlane said.
The Australian government has forecast average domestic product (GDP) to rise 3.75 percent through to June 30, 1998, up from 3.25 percent through 1996/97.
"The manufacturing industry is growing relatively sedately," Macfarlane said.
Last year, Amcor reported its first annual profit fall in more than a decade and it has said it expected to report a further profit fall in the year to June 30, 1997.
Macfarlane said in terms of volume, Amcor's business is growing, but sales are not increasing due to pricing pressures.
